title: Help
intro: Flex Draw draws shapes and shows you how they look as text. Here you find the basics, with pictures.

draw.title: 1. Draw
draw.text: Pick a tool and drag on the canvas to paint something.
draw.alt: A yellow rectangle, next to a pencil with a red stroke

select.title: 2. Select
select.text: Click a shape. A dashed frame shows that it is selected.
select.alt: A teal rectangle with a dashed frame and a mouse pointer

colour.title: 3. Change the colour
colour.text: Click a colour in the palette. The selected shape gets this colour straight away.
colour.alt: Three colour swatches, the middle one is chosen, and a teal circle below

save.title: 4. Save
save.text: Download your picture as an SVG file. Ctrl + S works too.
save.alt: A document labelled SVG and an arrow pointing down

select.name: Select
select.text: Click a shape to select it.
select.alt: A mouse pointer over a shape with a dashed selection frame

rect.name: Rectangle
rect.text: Drag to draw a rectangle. With Shift it becomes a square.
rect.alt: A yellow rectangle with red corner points

ellipse.name: Ellipse
ellipse.text: Drag to draw an ellipse. With Shift it becomes a circle.
ellipse.alt: A teal ellipse inside a dashed frame

polygon.name: Polygon
polygon.text: Click point by point. A double-click closes the shape.
polygon.alt: Points joined by lines to form a polygon

freehand.name: Freehand
freehand.text: Draw freely. Your line becomes a smooth curve.
freehand.alt: A wavy line that starts with a red dot

pan.name: Pan
pan.text: Hold the Space bar and drag, or drag with the middle mouse button.
pan.alt: Four arrows pointing in all directions

zoom.name: Zoom
zoom.text: Turn the mouse wheel, or use + , − and 100 %.
zoom.alt: A magnifying glass with a plus sign

combine.title: Combine shapes
combine.intro: Two shapes overlap. One rule decides which parts stay. The square is the first shape, the circle the second.
combine.before: Before: a square and a circle overlap

unite.name: Unite
unite.text: Both shapes become one single shape. Nothing gets lost.
unite.alt: After: the square and the circle as one shared shape

intersect.name: Intersect
intersect.text: Only the part where both shapes overlap stays.
intersect.alt: After: only the overlap of the square and the circle

subtract.name: Subtract
subtract.text: The circle is cut out of the square. What stays is the square without the circle.
subtract.alt: After: the square with a piece of circle missing

exclude.name: Exclude
exclude.text: Only the outer parts stay. The overlap disappears.
exclude.alt: After: the square and the circle without the part where they overlap

teacher.title: For teachers
teacher.text: The four rules match SQL joins. Each shape is a table, and each overlap is a match:
items: Unite = FULL JOIN (all rows of both tables)
Intersect = INNER JOIN (only rows with a match)
Subtract = LEFT JOIN, but only the rows without a match
Exclude = FULL JOIN without the overlap

svg.title: What is SVG?
svg.text: SVG stands for “Scalable Vector Graphics”. An SVG picture is not a photo, it is text: every shape is one line of code. A circle, for example, has a centre (cx and cy) and a radius (r). The browser draws the picture from this text, and the editor writes this text for you while you draw.
svg.codeLabel: This is the text for this smiley:
svg.alt: A drawn smiley: a yellow circle with two eyes and a red mouth

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.caption: Keyboard shortcuts in the editor
shortcuts.mac: On a Mac, use Cmd (⌘) instead of Ctrl.

rows.move: Move the selection, with Shift in bigger steps
